issues.body:
Candidate: rambergite (MnS), distinct from alabandite, amorphous manganese sulfide and rhodochrosite. Lee et al. (2011), *Manganese sulfide formation via concomitant microbial manganese oxide and thiosulfate reduction*, Environmental Microbiology13:3275–3288, DOI10.1111/j.1462-2920.2011.02587.x, PMID21951417, PNNL-SA-69040.

Round76 verified PubMed/Crossref/PNNL metadata, queried OSTI by DOI and report number (record1115855), and checked OpenAlex. OSTI supplies a citation link only; its journal-name metadata disagrees with PubMed/Crossref. Wiley full-text and the advertised supplementary TableS1 route returned403 HTML. No original main paper or real supplementary DOC was acquired; retained responses are not evidence of methods/figures access. The abstract mentions MR-1, cytochrome mutants, MnO2/thiosulfate and donor-dependent products, but these are discovery leads only.

Acceptance: obtain a legitimate complete14-page original and actual associated SI, record URL/version/hash/bytes; independently inspect all claim-bearing diffraction/microscopy/chemical data and supplementary modeling. Verify γ-MnS phase assignment, organisms/strain/mutants, substrate preparation, donor/medium/loading/pH, no-cell and indirect-sulfide controls, time course and replicate scope. Preserve mixed carbonate products, nulls and alternative routes; distinguish biomineralization from recovery. Curate only claims supported after independent review. No rambergite owner was added from the abstract. This source gap does not invalidate the separately accepted abiotic copper-sulfide records.

Research dossier: `research/sources/round76-sulfides/20261014T163419Z-source-investigation.md` (round76 working branch; publication pending).
issues.title: Acquire Lee 2011 originals and supplements before rambergite curation

issues.body:
Leads: Cheng and Hu2007, *Bioleaching of anilite using pure and mixed culture of Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans and Acidithiobacillus caldus*, Minerals Engineering20:1187–1190, DOI10.1016/j.mineng.2007.05.001; Cheng et al.2008, *Bioleaching of anilite by Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans*, Transactions of Nonferrous Metals Society of China18:1410–1414, DOI10.1016/S1003-6326(09)60017-0.

Round76 read publisher abstracts/partial sections and the official journal2008 page, verified2008 Crossref metadata, and followed its advertised citation_pdf_url https://tnmsc.csu.edu.cn/EN/PDF/768. That route returned HTTP200 with zero bytes, not a PDF. The2007 publisher offers purchase/access and incomplete sections; no complete original graphics were acquired. Shared authors and similar conditions require experiment-lineage checking. The journal2008 HTML publication-date metadata says June25 whereas Crossref/publisher bibliographic context gives the December issue; do not silently equate metadata date with experimental date.

Acceptance: acquire complete originals4 and5pages and relevant SI if present; verify feed diffraction after grinding (anilite can transform to digenite), mixed phases, organisms/isolates, biomass state, FeSO4·7H2O versus elemental Fe concentration denominators, sulfur additions, inoculum, abiotic/iron-free/no-sulfur controls, replication and Cu assay. Preserve reported no-effect arms and distinguish sulfur-rich EDAX signals from phase-confirmed elemental sulfur. Determine overlap between papers rather than counting them as independent replication. The current anilite owner is explicitly abiotic and may remain so. Digenite Ruan2013 DOI10.1016/j.mineng.2013.01.002 and van der Graaf2020 DOI10.3390/microorganisms8091275 remain separately bounded prior-round leads: mixed or chalcocite-labeled patterns must not establish digenite-specific microbial activity.

Research dossier: `research/sources/round76-sulfides/20261014T163419Z-source-investigation.md` (round76 working branch; publication pending).
issues.title: Acquire phase-resolved microbial anilite originals before extending its abiotic record
